    Model Calibration

    This isn't machine learning — it's a straightforward check: does each confidence tier's real bias (actual minus projected) get fed back into future projections? Only after MIN_SAMPLE=30 real graded entries for that exact stat+tier, and even then only by 30% of the measured gap (never a full overcorrection off one hot or cold stretch).

    Confidence calibration (Highest Confidence ranking)

    Checks whether the stated confidence on Best 5 picks actually means what it claims -- does an "80% confident" pick really hit 80% of the time, or is the model running overconfident? Same real technique as touchdown probability shrink above, applied to each yardage stat's real graded history. A shrink factor below 1.0x means real results have been less extreme than the raw math claimed, and the displayed confidence gets pulled back toward 50% by that real amount.

    Signal effectiveness

    Real check on whether the newer context signals (usage trend, target share trend, next-man-up flags, recent-form matchups, injury status) actually correlate with real outcomes -- not assumed, checked directly. Compares the real hit rate of picks tagged with each signal against picks without it, requiring at least 20 real graded picks on both sides before showing a real difference. Once a signal shows a genuine, repeatable gap here, it's a real candidate to fold into the actual projection math -- until then, it stays informational only, same discipline as every other calibration check on this page.

    Prediction Accuracy Over Time

    The dashed line marks 50% -- a coin flip. If the model is genuinely useful, dots should trend up and away from it as more weeks accumulate, not stay flat around it. NFL's weekly cadence means this fills in one point per week, not per day -- an honestly short series right now, not a lesser one.

    Projection accuracy — every player who played

    Hit/miss needs a market line, and some picks never get one. This scores all of them on how close our projection was to what really happened. Typical miss is the average gap (smaller is better); bias is the average signed gap (positive = we projected too low). Players who did not play are left out rather than scored as a 0 (0 excluded so far). The trend compares the first and latest week only, so with a few weeks of data treat it as a hint, not a verdict.

    Best 5 Track Record

    Two different questions, tracked separately, same as the accuracy-by-tier split above. Highest Confidence is the model's own most-likely-to-hit ranking — real probability, using each player's own game-to-game variance (or real Poisson probability for touchdowns). Best Value is the biggest gap between our projection and the real market line — where the market looks most wrong. These can and often will name different players in the same week. The goal stated in the project brief: watch these numbers climb toward a consistent 4/5 or 5/5 week over week, not just show a good week once.

    Is the Best 5 actually better than the site's other picks?

    For each prop, the hit rate of the Best 5 picks next to every other graded pick that had a real line. If Best 5 is genuinely finding the better calls, its number should sit clearly above the other one. With fewer than 20 picks on either side the gap is mostly luck, so the page says “too early” instead of declaring a winner.

    Team Markets

    Real game-outcome predictions — moneyline, spread and total — frozen from our own real net-points-per-game model against FanDuel's real line at that same moment, then graded against the real final score once the game finishes. A real tie (moneyline) or a pick frozen with no real FanDuel line to compare against counts as graded once the game is final, but never counts toward the hit rate — there's nothing real to call it right or wrong against. This week's ranked picks live on Matchups; this is the full real history.

    Signal Effectiveness

    Does a real context signal (EPA edge, recent form, injury edge, rest edge) actually predict which real picks hit, or does it just look plausible? Compares the real hit rate of graded picks WITH each signal against picks WITHOUT it, gated at 20+ real graded GAMES on both sides (each game counts once, even though it carries a moneyline, spread and total pick). "Insufficient data" just means not enough real games yet; "untestable" means every game so far has had the same value, so there is nothing to compare against until that changes.
